haiku-low.q1: MySQL commits first, with the pending row in the same transaction. Then the Postgres copy runs before the response, with a short timeout. If Postgres fails, the request still succeeds; the sweep retries.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the target has no tombstone for the id and its row has a lower version. Otherwise the copy does nothing, or inserts only if no row exists.
haiku-low.q3: Every instance must show write_mode dual before the backfill is enqueued. Flags refresh every 30 seconds. The document states no longer bound on disagreement.
haiku-low.q4: Each batch waits while mysql_replica_lag_seconds exceeds 5, rechecking every 10 seconds. Batches are 2,000 rows, read from the replica, in id order.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: a clean comparison, then read_from_pg steps of 1, 10, 50, 100 percent, each held 24 hours, with no Postgres read errors. Source: reads at 100% for 3 days, comparer clean, manual start.
haiku-low.q6: A pending row, kept in the source database and written in the same transaction as the change. The sweep runs every minute, copies the row, and deletes the pending row if its version still matches.
haiku-low.q7: Erases write tombstones in both databases, never removed, and the copy rule does nothing when a tombstone exists. The document still lists a gap: a backfill insert can reappear until the sweep removes it.
haiku-low.q8: Progress is a MySQL row with last_id, done flag and heartbeat, saved in one transaction after each batch copy. It stops when a batch is empty, then sets done.
haiku-low.q9: The comparer compares both tables id by id, 2,000 per batch. For each difference, it rereads the MySQL primary row; if still different, it applies the copy rule and counts a mismatch.
haiku-low.q10: Writes pause (503) and the switch waits until every instance shows paused, then pg_primary. If not every instance shows pg_primary within 75 seconds, write_mode returns to dual. NOT STATED for any other mixed-mode guard.
haiku-low.q11: After the switch, the Postgres sequence assigns new ids, set to the larger max id plus 1,000,000. On rollback, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT gets the same offset, avoiding collisions.
haiku-low.q12: Postgres copies every write to MySQL for 14 days, with a clean Postgres-to-MySQL comparison. Rollback: pause, sweep Postgres pending, set AUTO_INCREMENT, set dual. Allowed only before step 9 starts.

sonnet.q1: MySQL is committed first (with the pending row in the same transaction), then in the same request before the response the copy rule runs in Postgres with a short timeout. If Postgres fails or times out, the request still succeeds; the pending row stays and the sweep retries.
sonnet.q2: Only if the incoming row has a higher version than the existing row (existing row's version is lower), and the target has no tombstone for that id. Otherwise nothing happens. It runs in one transaction that locks the user id in the target.
sonnet.q3: Every instance must show write_mode `dual` (app_flag_value metric) before the operator enqueues the backfill. Instances refresh flags every 30 seconds, so they can disagree for up to about 30 seconds (the doc says each step waits until all show the new value).
sonnet.q4: Before each batch it waits while mysql_replica_lag_seconds is above 5 (rechecking every 10 seconds). It reads from the replica rather than the primary, in batches of up to 2,000 rows in id order. (The doc names no other throttle.)
sonnet.q5: Reads: a clean comparison (a full pass with zero mismatches and no pending rows in MySQL); then ramp 1, 10, 50, 100 percent, each step waiting 24 hours with the comparer still clean and no Postgres read errors. Source of truth (step 7, manual): reads at 100% for at least 3 days and the comparer clean; then pause writes, wait 10 s, sweep until pending is empty in MySQL (and none in Postgres), set the sequence, then switch to pg_primary.
sonnet.q6: A pending row (user id, version, erased flag) records it. It is kept in the source database (MySQL before step 7), written in the same transaction as the change. The sweep, running every minute, copies the current source row (or tombstone) to the other database and then deletes the pending row if the version still matches.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones: every erase writes a tombstone in both databases, never removed, and the copy rule does nothing if the target has a tombstone for the id. Backfill also skips ids with pending or tombstone rows on the MySQL primary. Known gap (open question): a backfill copy that began before the erase committed can re-insert the row in Postgres if the erase's Postgres copy also fails; the sweep removes it within about a minute.
sonnet.q8: In the job progress row in MySQL (last_id, done flag, heartbeat). After copying a batch, last_id is set to the batch's highest id and the heartbeat updated in one MySQL transaction, so it only advances after the copy; if Postgres fails, last_id isn't saved and the batch is retried (re-copying is harmless). It stops when a batch is empty, then sets done.
sonnet.q9: The comparer compares both tables id by id in id order. For each differing id it re-reads the row from the MySQL primary; if it still differs, it applies the copy rule and counts a mismatch. Ids missing on both sides or tombstoned in Postgres are not mismatches. Passes repeat until one has zero mismatches and no pending rows.
sonnet.q10: It sets write_mode to `paused` first (writes get a retryable 503) and waits until every instance shows it, so no instance writes in either order during the change; then it waits 10 s, sweeps, sets the sequence, and sets pg_primary, waiting until all instances show it. If not every instance shows pg_primary within 75 seconds of substep 1, set write_mode back to `dual` (MySQL is complete, nothing lost). The pause must stay under 90 seconds.
sonnet.q11: Postgres, via its id sequence. Collisions are avoided by setting the sequence to the larger of the two tables' max ids plus 1,000,000 (step 7). Copies to MySQL keep the ids given. On rollback, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is set to the larger of the two max ids plus 1,000,000 (R-1 substep 3).
sonnet.q12: Each create/update/erase commits in Postgres with its pending row, then the copy rule runs in MySQL in the same request; the sweep retries failures, and a Postgres-to-MySQL comparer must stay clean. Rollback (R-1): pause writes, sweep until Postgres pending is empty, set MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT, set write_mode to dual, clear the migration-state time (reads stay on Postgres). The option lasts at least 14 days and ends when step 9 (pg_only) starts; rollback is only allowed before step 9.
